Worker-prompt lessons (binding for dispatch prompts):- Mathematical notation in prose uses LaTeX per `.jit/reference/content-standards.md` (`$\mathrm{GF}(2^m)$`, `$O(n^2)$`, `$r < 1$`); code identifiers stay in code spans. - Every command uses the AGENTS.md forms: `./scripts/cargo-budget.sh cargo ...`; tests `./scripts/cargo-budget.sh --test cargo nextest run ...`. - External works and standards cite registry keys `@/citation/<key>` from `.jit/references.toml` (resolve with `jit item show`). - No timing, speed or feasibility statement without a commit-pinned receipt; performance figures appear only on `docs/reference/performance-evidence.md`, and other pages link its anchors. - State exactly what a check or guarantee establishes (probabilistic vs exact; which binary flushes on which signal); verify each behavioral claim against code or by running it. - A universal statement ("every claim", "all paths") must hold for every case on the page. - Records hold no hand-copied counts: commit raw outputs as files and cite them with the exact commands; show equality with a `diff` whose empty output the record states. - Facts owned by another page are linked, not restated (installation and per-crate features: `docs/reference/supported-configurations.md`; architecture: `docs/concepts/acceleration-architecture.md`; field families: `docs/concepts/finite-field-arithmetic.md`). - Crate READMEs follow the rules in `the README rules note below` and state capabilities per area naming at most public modules, never type or function inventories. - Index rows in `docs/index.md` go into the section's existing `| Page | ... |` table. - Digest-pinned inputs (protocols, preregistrations, addenda, schemas, receipts, `inputs/` snapshots) keep their bytes. - Never commit `__pycache__` or build output.

README rules: R1 Rendered Rustdoc link: `[Rustdoc](../../target/doc/<crate_underscored>/index.html)` next to `./scripts/cargo-budget.sh cargo doc -p <crate> --no-deps`. A `src/lib.rs` link alone fails REQ-03. R2 Feature table: keep one line per feature, but state its authority right above it: "The `[features]` table of [`Cargo.toml`](Cargo.toml) is authoritative." (@/inv/single-source-prose; an uncited manual inventory fails). R3 Module/identifier names: name only public paths (`gf2_core::BitVec`, public modules). Private modules re-exported at the root (e.g. gf2-core `bitvec`, `bitslice`) are not "modules" to an adopter; check `pub mod` vs `mod` in src/lib.rs. R4 Installation: no layout-dependent `path = "crates/<crate>"` snippet. Link the single installation source instead: `[installation](../../docs/reference/supported-configurations.md#installation)` (the page lands on main from branch worktree-agent-2ff9953a; docs-mechanical may flag the link until it merges — expected). R5 Commands in AGENTS.md form only (`./scripts/cargo-budget.sh cargo ...`, tests `./scripts/cargo-budget.sh --test cargo nextest run -p <crate> --cargo-profile ci-test --profile ci`). R6 External works and standards cite `@/citation/<key>` from .jit/references.toml.

Session 4 (2026-10-03): owner interviewed on all ten open questions; rulings are in escalations. Standing rules: sweep units must be net-negative in lines per unit unless each added line is a missing panic, safety or contract statement listed in the unit's record; models: opus for Rust, scripts, permanent prose and reworks, sonnet for moves, inventories and records, no fable; the lead never pushes.

README rules superseded 2026-10-03: a crate README states purpose and when to choose the crate, plus links (docs/index.md, owning reference/concepts pages, generated Rustdoc link with its cargo doc command). No capability list, feature table or module inventory (R2 and R3 lapse; R1, R4, R5, R6 stand).

jit issue create for orphan tasks needs --orphan; filed roadmap issues default to ready, set backlog explicitly.
Do not add a dependency from a new task onto a story: deps define containment.

jit issue create --orphan does not satisfy repository integrity: a new issue with no dependency edge fails jit validate (isolated issue). Wire every filed issue into a container immediately; parenting into another epic needs owner approval.

Never `git add .jit` blindly: another session's tracker writes ride along (ab6b6b09b swept in the 6dc81018 archive). Inspect `git status --short .jit` and stage only this epic's files plus events.jsonl/index.
A container archive copies documents that a non-terminal issue also owns; content-identity lookups then see duplicates (62ce5927). Run cargo-ci after any archive lands on main.

Reviewer recomputation can be wrong (62f0d0e6 F2 pattern counts; an independent grep confirmed the record). Do not argue: make the record reproducible at the named commit so the reviewer runs the script itself.

dispatch-worker-worktree.sh stops at the first branch collision after creating earlier worktrees; delete merged worktree-agent-* branches first and verify `git worktree list` shows every worktree before dispatching (three workers were sent to missing worktrees).

scripts/cargo-ci.sh exports a scratch TMPDIR; an sccache server first started inside a CI run keeps it after deletion and every later compile fails with 'Failed to create temp dir' (e250b5bb). Before a gate batch: `sccache --stop-server; sccache --start-server` from a normal shell.

A record that names a measured commit must give a reproduction that compares a fresh run at that commit against the files of the record's commit, not the files checked out at the measured commit (62f0d0e6 round 2).
